A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoAM research. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and Appendices A–D are readable and matchable despite the added discussion and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original annotation-quality analyses, MWE identification experiments in Section 6, and input-format and definition ablations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds an analysis of human annotations against finalized CoAM labels in Section 7 and Table 8.

M1.justification: CoAM construction, MWE type tagging, CAIGen, MaW, and LLM fine-tuning procedures are unchanged. The added recommendation to train annotators adequately does not establish a change to the annotation procedure actually used.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English CoAM sources and MWE identification task, alongside the DiMSUM consistency audit. The added human analysis reuses the existing corpus and annotators without introducing new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 7 and Table 8 add humans as a measured reference for comparison with automated systems, explicitly discussing Qwen-72B. The MaW variants, Llama/Qwen models, and FT/FSL/ZSL comparisons remain unchanged. The human reference uses different sentence coverage from the model evaluation.

E3.justification: The new human analysis treats raw annotations as predictions and final CoAM annotations as gold, covering both training and test sets. This adds an evaluation protocol; existing model splits, metrics, training budgets, and settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a diagnostic analysis asking whether low recall and discontinuity difficulties also characterize humans, with recall breakdowns by continuity and WordNet membership and selected individual-annotator results. Existing model-error analyses, examples, and main-text and appendix ablations are retained.

E5.justification: The retained experiments use the same three-run/seed information and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. The new human analysis supplies point estimates and selected annotator scores without introducing uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or additional repeated-run information.

E6.justification: Table 8 adds human F1/precision/recall of 56.5/64.5/51.0%, with continuous/discontinuous recall of 52.1/41.8%; Section 7 also reports individual-annotator scores. The introduction corrects Qwen-72B recall from 50.7% to 52.8%, which Table 6 already reported in v2. Existing model and appendix result values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal task representation, MWE definitions, and exact-match metric formulas in Appendix B.2 are unchanged. No theoretical result, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain CoAM, MWE type annotations, and CAIGen. Both versions claim that fine-tuned Qwen-72B outperforms MaW while recall remains low; the shortened conclusion and corrected recall number do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the human results as motivation for better training and modeling of discontinuous MWEs. It acknowledges that raw annotations contribute to the gold labels and that annotators worked on different sentences, assuming similar difficulty. Section 4.5 also adds an annotator-training recommendation; the existing Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: Preprocessing, annotation instructions, prompts, hyperparameters, greedy decoding, hardware, runtimes, and dataset/code access information are unchanged. Appendices A–D match after accounting for table and footnote renumbering.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to earlier MWE datasets and systems remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 inserts Section 7 Discussion before the renumbered conclusion and makes limited wording edits in the introduction, annotation discussion, results discussion, and conclusion. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the human-results Table 8, removes incorrect bold highlighting from Rule's type-specific recalls in Table 6a, and replaces 'Ours' with 'CAIGen' in Table 1. Subsequent tables are renumbered and text reflows; existing figures and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The new human analysis provides useful context for low recall and discontinuity errors, while the recall correction and Table 6a highlighting improve reporting accuracy. Its implications remain limited by different sentence coverage and the contribution of human annotations to the gold labels, so the training-related interpretations are suggestive. These are modest gains; the corpus, methods, and primary and appendix evaluations remain unchanged.
